e-9454.knowledge_point: Calculating the Force Acting on a Body Given Its Velocity
e-9454.problem:
A body of mass $3 \, \textrm{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons $(\textrm{N}).$
At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t) =t^2- e^{t-4}$ meters per second.
Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t=4$ seconds.
e-9454.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-{e}^{t-4}) \\  & =2t-{e}^{t-4}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=4 \, \textrm{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =2(4)-{e}^{4-4} \\  & =8-1 \\  & =7\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =3\cdot (7) \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F| = |21| = 21 \, \textrm{N}.
$$

e-9859.knowledge_point: Calculating the Force Acting on a Body Given Its Displacement
e-9859.problem:
A body of mass $2 \, \textrm{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t) = e^{3t-6} + t^2$ meters. Find the expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
e-9859.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t-6}+{t}^{2}) \\  & =3{e}^{3t-6}+2t\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{e}^{3t-6}+2t) \\  & =9{e}^{3t-6}+2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force acting on the body, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =2\cdot (9{e}^{3t-6}+2) \\  & =18{e}^{3t-6}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

e-9860.knowledge_point: Determining Moments When a Force Has Zero Magnitude
e-9860.problem:
A body of mass $2 \, \textrm{kg}$ moves in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\geq 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t) =2t^3-12t^2-30t+5$ meters per second.
Calculate the time when the force acting on the body has a magnitude of zero.
e-9860.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-12{t}^{2}-30t+5) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-24t-30\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{t}^{2}-24t-30 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}-4t-5 & =0 \\ (t+1)(t-5) & =0 \\ t & =-1,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t \geq 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude when $t=5 \, \textrm{s}.$

content.problem:
A body of mass $6\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}$ meters per second.
Find an expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-{t}^{2}) \\  & =3{t}^{2}-2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =6\cdot (3{t}^{2}-2t) \\  & =18{t}^{2}-12t.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}+{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4t-{e}^{5-t}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4-(-{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4+{e}^{5-t}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=5\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =4+{e}^{5-5} \\  & =4+1 \\  & =5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =4\cdot (5) \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F|=|20|=20\,\text{N}.
$$

content.problem:
A body of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons $(\text{N}).$
At time $t$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=2{t}^{2}+{e}^{5-t}$ meters.
Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t=5$ seconds.
content.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}+{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4t-{e}^{5-t}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4-(-{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4+{e}^{5-t}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=5\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =4+{e}^{5-5} \\  & =4+1 \\  & =5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =4\cdot (5) \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F|=|20|=20\,\text{N}.
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
A body of mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=t-4\sqrt{t}$ meters.
Find the expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-4\sqrt{t}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-4{t}^{1/2}) \\  & =1-4\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot {t}^{-1/2} \\  & =1-2{t}^{-1/2}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2{t}^{-1/2}) \\  & =0-2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})\cdot {t}^{-3/2} \\  & ={t}^{-3/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{t\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =5\cdot (\frac{1}{t\sqrt{t}}) \\  & =\frac{5}{t\sqrt{t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity v(t), we differentiate the displacement s(t):

v(t)=dsdt=ddt(t−4t)=ddt(t−4t1/2)=1−4⋅12⋅t−1/2=1−2t−1/2

F=ma=5⋅(1tt)=5tt.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-36t+2$ meters per second.
Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.
after.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-36t+2) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-6t-36\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{t}^{2}-6t-36 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}-t-6 & =0 \\ (t-3)(t+2) & =0 \\ t & =-2,\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\ge 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at $t=3\,\text{s}.$

Question 12
?

A body of mass 5kg is moving in a straight line along the x-axis under the action of a single force F, measured in Newtons. At time t≥0 seconds, the position of the body is given by s(t)=t4−150t2+8 meters. Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.

a
t=8s
b
t=6s
c
t=5s
d
t=3s
e
t=2s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

According to Newton’s second law F=ma, where F is the force, m is the mass, and a is the acceleration.

To find the velocity v(t), we differentiate the displacement s(t):

v(t)=dsdt=ddt(t4−150t2+8)=4t3−300t

To find the acceleration a(t), we differentiate the velocity v(t):

a(t)=dvdt=ddt(4t3−300t)=12t2−300

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set a(t)=0 and solve for t:

12t2−300=012t2=300t2=25t=±5

Since t≥0, we disregard the negative solution.

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at t=5s.

content.problem:
A body of mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)={t}^{4}-150{t}^{2}+8$ meters.
Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.
content.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-150{t}^{2}+8) \\  & =4{t}^{3}-300t\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}-300t) \\  & =12{t}^{2}-300\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}12{t}^{2}-300 & =0 \\ 12{t}^{2} & =300 \\ {t}^{2} & =25 \\ t & =\pm 5\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\ge 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at $t=5\,\text{s}.$

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
A body of mass $1.5\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=2{t}^{3}-12{t}^{2}+t-5$ meters per second.
Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.
after.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-12{t}^{2}+t-5) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-24t+1\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2}-24t+1) \\  & =12t-24\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}12t-24 & =0 \\ 12 & =24 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at $t=2\,\text{s}.$
